requirements.text: If no alert notification exists, send an alert-type notification to the assigned user with the following message

cells.message: A backup failure has been detected for the development database, and your immediate review is required to verify backup integrity, confirm whether recent jobs are still failing, and update the incident with your findings so we can determine any further risk to customer-facing systems.

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_021' AND email = 'sophie.mueller@acme.com' AND type = 'alert' AND status = 'sent' AND message = 'A backup failure has been detected for the development database, and your immediate review is required to verify backup integrity, confirm whether recent jobs are still failing, and update the incident with your findings so we can determine any further risk to customer-facing systems.'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only notification the task creates
the development database backup failure incident is INC_021 ('Automated backup job failed for development database'), the only backup incident on the seed
INC_021 is assigned_to USER_008, Sophie Mueller, an active user whose directory email is sophie.mueller@acme.com
the send is required: INC_021 has no notification of any type on the seed
message is the request's quoted text verbatim, including the hyphen in 'customer-facing'
status sent kept from the benchmark check; consistent with the request's 'successfully sent'
subject and org_id not fixed by request or policy; not tested

requirements.text: create a new proactive Problem record to review the resilience and reliability of development database backup processes, and assign this Problem to the same user identified as the incident assignee
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_003' AND assigned_to = 'USER_008' AND status = 'new' AND org_id = 'ORG_002' AND problem_statement LIKE '%backup%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (PRB_003 after PRB_002); the benchmark anchors on number = 'PRB0000002', a server-kept column, replaced by the id
status not stated; policy 4.2 sets every new Problem to status = new
org_id follows the incident, the assignee and the acting user, all ORG_002
the request fixes the subject (development database backup processes), not the wording; the statement must mention backup
impact, urgency, priority, category, opened_by and original_task are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested

requirements.text: retrieve the details of the development database backup failure incident (boundary: the other development database incident)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE incident_id = 'INC_009'
assumptions: INC_009 (slow queries on the development database, category database, assigned to USER_009) is the near match a loose reading of the description would pick; it has no notification on the seed and must get none

verify_new_db_backup_alert_sent_to_sophi.evidence: the request's quoted message ends 'risk to customer-facing systems' (hyphenated); the check's literal reads 'customer facing systems', so an agent sending the message as given would fail it. Message corrected to the request's text; incident INC_021, recipient sophie.mueller@acme.com, type alert and status sent kept, and the row anchored on NOTIF_008, the next id

verify_problem_assigned_to_incident_owne.evidence: anchored on number = 'PRB0000002', a server-kept column that is never a cell; replaced by problem_id = 'PRB_003' (next in sequence). assigned_to = 'USER_008' kept, matching INC_021's assignee on the seed. The check's description repeats the notification check's; its query tests the problem assignment

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a requirement that the new problem's original_task is INC_021, from policy 4.2's rule that a Problem must link all affected Incidents; one pass has it, the other does not; dropped because the request calls the Problem proactive (a review of backup processes) and names no incident to link, the policy's incident_to_problem related list has no table in this schema, no listed tool writes the incident's problem column, and the benchmark does not test original_task.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that the existing ORG_002 problem PRB_002 (also assigned to USER_008) keeps its statement, status, original_task and assignee; one pass has it, the other does not; dropped because PRB_002 is tied to the task only by its assignee, nothing in the request's description of the new Problem sweeps it in, and rewriting it instead of creating one already fails the PRB_003 requirement.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that no notification is created for INC_009, the other development database incident; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because INC_009 is the near match a loose reading of 'the development database backup failure incident' picks, and an alert sent for both incidents would pass the anchored NOTIF_008 requirement while only this stay catches the second.
disagreement: value: the problem's org_id: one pass tests org_id = 'ORG_002', the other leaves it untested; chose ORG_002, the tighter predicate, because org_id is NOT NULL and the acting user, the incident INC_021 and the assignee USER_008 are all in ORG_002 on the seed.
disagreement: disposition: 'verify_problem_assigned_to_incident_owner': repaired in one pass, kept in the other; chose repaired, because the requirement replaces the check's anchor on the server-kept number PRB0000002 with problem_id PRB_003, which changes the check's predicate.
The first two sentences of the request (retrieve the incident, validate the assigned user) are read-only. The benchmark's number PRB0000002 agrees with the seed's per-organisation numbering (each organisation holds one PRB0000001), so the original check would likely pass on a correct run; the anchor is replaced only because number is server-kept. Policy 4.2's linking rule is recorded here for a reviewer who reads the proactive Problem as linked to INC_021: that reader would add original_task = 'INC_021' to the problem requirement. The acting user USER_007 is an active admin in ORG_002, so no role constraint bites.
